messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p95 latency spike and throughput drop observed in canary pool 'canary-eu-2' starting ~10m after rollout of release/2027.03.kernel-select. Automatic fallback to legacy kernel observed on ~30% of canary pods. Severity: high. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/runtime-degradation>.
Dana (oncall): Acknowledged. I'm on it — paging eng-runtime and SRE. Handing incident to on-call eng-runtime after initial triage.
Alice M (eng-runtime): I'm looking. Which kernel selector was active? Did we change the quantization path in this rollout?
Bob S (eng-runtime): The canary rollout shipped kernel-selection v3.2.3 which added avx512 fused kernels and a new batching heuristic. We saw fallback to scalar kernels (slow path) on ~25% of requests; also continuous eviction logs in the KV cache.
Carlos (sre): I'm seeing repeated OOMs in canary-eu-2 autoscaler group after traffic shifted. Pod restarts correlate with high token-per-second spikes. Could be a regressing memory growth pattern.
Eve (product): Any customer-facing impact identified? Any errors or 5xxs?
Dana (oncall): Customer impact: a small set of high-throughput customers saw increased tail latency and 502 spikes for short windows. SRE logs show ~18 errors/min at peak across 6 tenants. No billing regressions yet, but latency SLOs were missed.
Alice M (eng-runtime): Ok. Hypothesis: new kernel selection increases working set for certain seq-length distributions which breaks KV cache eviction policy, leading to fallbacks and stalls. Short-term mitigation: disable the new kernel selector and force old selector for canary pool.
Bob S (eng-runtime): I'll flip the safety flag for the canary pool now. Command:
```
# disable kernel-selection v3 for canary pool
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/feature-flags/disable \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"flag":"kernel-select-v3","scope":"canary-eu-2"}'
```
Alice M (eng-runtime): After flag flip, we'll restart the serving runtime on affected nodes to clear KV cache. Planning rolling restart with 1 node at a time.
deploy-bot: Action: feature-flag kernel-select-v3 disabled for scope=canary-eu-2 by Bob S. Change-id: ff-98431.
Carlos (sre): Initiating rolling restart. Watch for restart storms, using drain + cordon. Command I ran: `kubectl rollout restart ds/infer-runtime -n canary-eu-2 --field-selector spec.nodeName=...`
Dana (oncall): Coordinating with support to message impacted customers. Draft: "We observed increased latency during a canary deployment. We've reverted the canary selector and are monitoring. No action required on your side." @Eve can you sign off?
Eve (product): Looks good. Suggest adding ETA for full mitigation: ~15-25 minutes. Also log any tenants that request escalations.
Alice M (eng-runtime): After restart metrics: p95 down to baseline, throughput restored to pre-deploy levels. No further kernel fallbacks detected in canary pool. Continuing to monitor for 30m.
Dana (oncall): Monitoring window started. If stable for 30m we'll mark mitigated and schedule a postmortem.
Bob S (eng-runtime): Root cause notes (first pass): kernel-selection heuristic mis-classified a subset of sequence-length distributions, enabling an AVX path that isn't memory-safe under certain cache configs. We'll add additional guardrails in the selector and a unit test reproducer.
Carlos (sre): No customer escalations in the last 20m. Autoscaler metrics normalized.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: eng-runtime, SRE. Incident page: <https://redwood.incidents/INC-20712>.
Dana (oncall): On-call handoff in 40m to next shift; I'll include the mitigation steps and required follow-ups: 1) backport selector guard, 2) add a canary test with wide seq-length distribution, 3) update rollout checklist to include KV cache monitoring.
Alice M (eng-runtime): Agree. I'll file the postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks for quick responses everyone. :thumbsup:
